```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(reticulate)
library(tidyverse)
use_python(Sys.getenv("RETICULATE_PYTHON", unset = Sys.which("python3")), required = TRUE)
```

## Workflow

1. **Python (pymovements)**: load raw gaze samples, convert pixels to degrees, compute velocities, detect fixations and saccades.
2. **R (tidyverse, lme4)**: merge fixations with interest areas, compute reading measures (FFD, GD, TVT, ...), run statistics.

This mirrors the analysis in [fixated](https://github.com/bernhardangele/fixated), using pymovements for the preprocessing.

## Simulated raw data

```{python}
import numpy as np
import polars as pl

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
rows = []
t = 0
x, y = 100.0, 540.0
for target in [150, 260, 380, 470, 590, 700, 650, 800, 900]:
    for _ in range(int(rng.integers(40, 80))):  # fixation, 1000 Hz
        rows.append((t, target + rng.normal(0, 1), 540 + rng.normal(0, 1)))
        t += 1
    for k in range(1, 21):  # saccade
        rows.append((t, x + (target - x) * k / 20, 540.0))
        t += 1
    x = target
samples = pl.DataFrame(rows, schema=["time", "x_pix", "y_pix"], orient="row")
samples.head()
```

## Preprocessing with pymovements

```{python}
import pymovements as pm

experiment = pm.Experiment(
    screen_width_px=1920, screen_height_px=1080,
    screen_width_cm=53, screen_height_cm=30,
    distance_cm=60, sampling_rate=1000,
)
gaze = pm.Gaze(
    samples=samples, experiment=experiment,
    time_column="time", time_unit="ms",
    pixel_columns=["x_pix", "y_pix"],
)
gaze.pix2deg()
gaze.pos2vel("savitzky_golay", degree=2, window_length=7)
gaze.detect("ivt", velocity_threshold=30)
gaze.compute_event_properties(["location", "duration"])
fixations = gaze.events.frame.filter(pl.col("name") == "fixation")
fixations.head()
```

## Handing over to R

```{python}
fix_df = fixations.select(["onset", "offset", "duration", "location"]).with_columns(
    pl.col("location").list.get(0).alias("x"),
).drop("location").to_pandas()
```

```{r}
fix <- py$fix_df
head(fix)
```

## Reading measures in R

```{r}
# Interest areas (words) on the x axis, in pixels
words <- tibble(word = 1:5, start = c(100, 300, 450, 650, 850), end = c(300, 450, 650, 850, 1000))

fix <- fix |>
  mutate(word = map_int(x, \(px) { w <- words$word[px >= words$start & px < words$end]; if (length(w)) w[1] else NA_integer_ })) |>
  filter(!is.na(word))

measures <- fix |>
  arrange(onset) |>
  group_by(word) |>
  summarise(FFD = first(duration), TVT = sum(duration), n_fix = n(), .groups = "drop")
measures
```

## Statistics

```{r}
#| eval: false
# With real data (many participants/items) fit mixed models, e.g.:
# lmerTest::lmer(log(FFD) ~ frequency + (1 | subject) + (1 | item), data = measures)
```

## Visual world experiments

Load the same way, detect fixations with pymovements, then assign each fixation to an area of interest
(target, competitor, distractors) in R and aggregate proportions of looks in time bins
(`count()` by time bin and AOI), followed by growth curve or cluster-based analyses.
